title: Directional transfer from coherence to longitudinal polarization and algebraic storage in a transmon with Markovian dephasing and a glassy environment: A non-Markovian fractional renewal model
authors: Ruha Uğraş Erdoğan, Ferit Acar Savacı
abstract: We develop a completely positive and trace-preserving non-Markovian transmon model with longitudinal Markovian dephasing and transverse renewal events motivated by a glassy two-level-system environment. A microscopic Hamiltonian identifies coupling subspaces; a normalized Prabhakar waiting-time law phenomenologically coarse grains slow defect reconfigurations. Forward chronological renewal histories yield an exact map-level Volterra equation, a noncommuting kernel--resolvent master equation, and an equivalent drift-conjugated Caputo-type representation with its required initial-value term. Without energy relaxation, Pauli-space dynamics splits into two one-dimensional subspaces and a coupled $(σ_y,σ_z)$ subspace supporting directional transfer between coherence and longitudinal polarization; $σ_x$ polarization is renewal-insensitive. For heavy-tailed waiting times with $0<α<1$, branch-cut analysis gives a generic $t^{-α}$ storage tail in longitudinal polarization generated from initial coherence and $O(t^{-1-α})$ reverse transfer; constant-rate Poisson renewal yields pole-generated exponential decay. Independent zero-temperature relaxation at finite $T_1$ exponentially cuts off these tails when its rate is below twice the pure-dephasing rate. We compare independent inverse-Laplace reconstructions of the waiting-time density, memory kernel, and selected qubit-response components to assess numerical accuracy. For the studied parameters, Prabhakar renewal gives larger forward-transfer magnitudes at the prescribed readout than both a scale-matched constant-rate Poisson reference and an inhomogeneous Poisson reference matching the full expected-count profile, including finite-$T_1$ tests. Both Poisson references yield larger evaluated finite-window peaks. Disorder-motivated renewal memory reshapes transmon decoherence selectively by state and direction.
summary: This paper develops a non-Markovian model for transmon decoherence caused by a glassy environment modeled via a fractional renewal process. It shows that the coupling to this disordered bath leads to directional polarization transfer with characteristic algebraic decay tails. The findings highlight that the specific memory structure of the disorder selectively reshapes the qubit's decoherence dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how decoherence in a transmon qubit can be selectively 'reshaped' by coupling to a complex, disordered environment modeled by Two-Level Systems (TLS).
main_result: The model predicts directional persistence in polarization transfer ($\sigma_y 	o \sigma_z$) characterized by algebraic long-time tails ($t^{-\alpha}$), which are distinct from predictions based on simple Poissonian noise models.
method: The analysis employs non-Markovian quantum dynamics, utilizing a fractional renewal framework derived from a Prabhakar waiting-time law to model the glassy environment.
model_or_system: The system is a transmon qubit coupled to a longitudinal Markovian bath and a transverse TLS environment. The dynamics are governed by a non-Markovian master equation derived from a fractional renewal process.
key_observables: Directional transfer between coherence ($\sigma_y$) and longitudinal polarization ($\sigma_z$), and the algebraic decay tails ($t^{-\alpha}$ for forward transfer).
important_parameters: The fractional exponent $\alpha$ ($0 < \alpha < 1$), the pure-dephasing rate ($\Gamma_Z$), and the energy relaxation rate ($\Gamma_1$).
main_assumptions: The environment is modeled by a glassy TLS system whose switching rates are coarse-grained using a Prabhakar waiting-time law, and the dynamics are treated as a combination of Markovian and renewal processes.
figures_summary: The notes refer to Figure 1, which conceptually illustrates the sequential action of longitudinal Markovian dephasing and transverse TLS kicks governed by independent Prabhakar waiting times.
paper_structure: The paper develops the non-Markovian model, derives the governing equations (Volterra/Caputo-type), analyzes the asymptotic behavior using branch-cut analysis for heavy-tailed waiting times, and compares results against standard Poissonian references.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated theoretical framework for understanding memory effects in superconducting qubits due to amorphous defects, moving beyond simple exponential decay models common in basic open quantum system treatments.
